newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A raft of dollar sellers carried the rand to its best level in two months on Monday in a market awash with the U.S. currency.
And dealers said the currency looked set to gain further ground in the short-term -- with many players predicting 4.55 by the end of the week.
At the local close the rand was pegged at 4.5825/5855 against the dollar from 4.6130/6180 at the close on Friday.
Dealers said that after initially softening to a day's weakest level of 4.6120 bid, the rand ran into dollar selling by both exporters and London-based banks.
They linked the selling to a report by London-based bank Union Bank of Switzerland, which said it expected the rand to appreciate strongly this year after taking account of inflation differentials.
"The UBS report was released on Friday but most of the guys only got to hear about it today," a currency trader said. "It impacted the local guys and the London banks," he added.
Local mining houses in particular had been keen to sell dollars on the day, the dealer said.

"On the basis of the rising trade surplus and the real interest rates, we continue to forecast dollar/rand at 4.8500 at year-end," UBS said, adding that this compared with a forward rate of 5.09 against the dollar.
By the end of the day, one-year forward rates had fallen to their lowest levels since October 21 when they stood at 45.30 basis points.
The one-year forward rate was last quoted at 45.75, translating into a rand/dollar exchange rate of about 5.04 twelve months hence.
The rand also continued to improve against the crosses, firming to a fresh three-month high against sterling, a nine-month high on the yen and an eight month-high against the German mark.
Dealers said the rand's gains against the other currencies was primarily a reflection of the dollar's resurgence against the three currencies.
The rand was last pegged at 7.4306/4378 against sterling from 7.5002/5138 on Friday, at 0.3570/3574 marks from 0.4565/3571 previously and at 26.03/26.07 yen from 25.78 at the end of last week.
The bond market rally also continued apace, with yields shaving another 10 basis points, bringing to nearly 80 the number of points the key R150 has fallen since January 2.
At the close the key R150 was quoted at 15.40 percent from 15.49 percent on Friday.
Dealers said that the main driving force behind gains on the gilts market was foreign demand.
Figures released by the Bond Exchange on Monday show foreigners were net buyers of 625.44 million rand's worth of bonds on Friday after buying 39.11 million rand on Thursday.
In the year so far, foreigners have bought nearly 1.4 billion rand's worth of bonds compared with 3.38 billion rand net purchases last year.

"The foreigners are looking for markets that are moving contra to their own and given what happened in our markets last year, we are a prime candidate for that," Chris Doyle, assistant general manager at UAL Merchant Bank Treasury said.

Dealers said that coupled with local interest, the buying was expected to nudge yields to 15.32 before targetting 15.25 -- a crucial chart point which analysts said could bring the lower 14.00 percent area into target range.
On the money market, Reserve Bank figures showed liquidity eased slightly at the weekend as the shortage dipped to 9.999 billion rand on 10.010 billion rand on Friday.

Demand for short-term paper helped three-month NCD rates lower to between 17.10 to 17.30 percent from 17.20 to 17.40 percent on Friday, while the 90-day BA rate was also lower at between 16.45 to 16.60 percent from 16.55 to 16.70 percent.
Nominal cumulative turnover on the bond market on Friday was 6.10 billion rand compared with 42.28 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
